title: Magnetic proximity beyond the interface: Layer-sequence-dependent exchange in WSe$_2$/CrI$_3$ heterostructures
authors: Natalie Kuhn, Marc Schütte, Joachim Emming, Felix Hellenkamp, Leo Dreyer, Frank Volmer, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Lutz Waldecker, Christoph Stampfer, Bernd Beschoten
abstract: Magnetic proximity effects in transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD)/2D-magnet heterostructures are often described in terms of the magnetization of the interfacial magnetic layer. Here, we show that this picture is sufficient to describe the neutral-exciton valley splitting of the TMD, but incomplete for its hole-doped electronic structure. We study a gate-tunable van der Waals heterostructure composed of monolayer WSe$_2$ in direct contact with trilayer CrI$_3$. By combining spatially and helicity-resolved reflection-contrast spectroscopy with magnetic circular dichroism, we identify two distinct magnetic domains in the trilayer CrI$_3$: one with purely antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling and one with a mixed antiferromagnetic (AFM)/ferromagnetic~(FM) coupling. In both domains, the sign of the neutral-exciton valley splitting of WSe$_2$ switches with the magnetization reversal of the adjacent CrI$_3$ layer. In contrast, helicity-resolved positive-trion spectroscopy of WSe$_2$ reveals a qualitatively different response. While the AFM domain shows a strongly helicity-selective trion resonance, the mixed AFM/FM domain exhibits trion resonances in both helicities. This behavior disappears when all CrI$_3$ layers are aligned in a parallel magnetization direction. Our results demonstrate that charged excitons are sensitive to the full layer-resolved magnetic sequence of the adjacent 2D-magnet, revealing magnetic proximity beyond the interface.
summary: This research investigates magnetic proximity effects in WSe2/CrI3 heterostructures, finding that the electronic response is not solely dictated by the interface magnetization. By comparing neutral exciton and trion spectroscopy across different magnetic domains, the authors demonstrate that the trion signal is sensitive to the full, layer-resolved magnetic sequence within the CrI3 stack, revealing magnetic coupling beyond the immediate interface.
main_problem: To determine if the magnetic proximity effect in WSe2/CrI3 heterostructures depends only on the magnetization of the interface or on the full, layer-resolved magnetic sequence of the adjacent magnetic layer.
main_result: The response of charged excitons (trions) is sensitive to the full layer-resolved magnetic sequence of the CrI3 trilayer, revealing magnetic proximity effects that extend beyond the immediate interface, unlike the neutral exciton splitting.
method: The study combines spatially and helicity-resolved spectroscopy (for neutral excitons and trions) with magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) to probe the magnetic domains and electronic response.
model_or_system: The system is a gate-tunable van der Waals heterostructure consisting of monolayer WSe2 coupled with a trilayer of CrI3. The magnetic state of the CrI3 is characterized by distinct domains exhibiting purely AFM or mixed AFM/FM interlayer coupling.
key_observables: Neutral-exciton valley splitting (Delta E), helicity-resolved positive-trion resonance ($	ext{X}^+$), and the magnetic hysteresis loops derived from MCD measurements.
important_parameters: Gate voltage ($V_g$) for hole doping, magnetic field ($B$), and the specific magnetic coupling sequence (AFM vs. mixed AFM/FM) within the CrI3 stack.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed electronic response (especially the trion) can be mapped to the underlying magnetic configuration of the multilayer stack.
figures_summary: Figures show spatial maps of exciton splitting, hysteresis loops for both neutral exciton splitting and MCD signals, and reconstructed layer-resolved magnetic configurations for the two identified magnetic domains.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical system and the limitations of simple interfacial models. It then uses spectroscopy to map out two distinct magnetic domains in the CrI3, characterizing their magnetic coupling. Finally, it contrasts the response of neutral excitons versus trions to demonstrate the layer-dependent magnetic proximity effect.
why_interesting: This work provides experimental evidence for magnetic coupling mechanisms in 2D heterostructures that depend on the stacking order of magnetic layers, which is crucial for designing next-generation spintronic and quantum computing components.
